patch.value: A release-completeness gate that requires every release tag to have a matching npm version and GitHub Release

A release is a triple: a git tag, a published npm version, and a GitHub Release. When an earlier release step failed, tags and npm versions accumulated with no GitHub Release and nothing reported the gap. This gate audits the three lists for every release tag, requiring both a matching published npm version and a matching GitHub Release, and refuses orphan npm versions and orphan GitHub Releases whose corresponding tag is missing. The analysis is separated from the I/O so the rules are driven by injected lists, and tests are hermetic with no network.

A release tag with no GitHub Release fails the gate; A release tag with no published npm version fails the gate; Orphan npm versions and orphan GitHub Releases fail the gate; The gate is wired into release:check like verify-release-publish-attestation

Detects the 14-day partial-release state that affected unbraind/pm-ops (v2026.08.28, v2026.08.29, v2026.08.31 published with no GitHub Release) and the same state in pm-context, pm-csv and pm-linear at v2026.08.09.

Wired into release:check via package.json. The 14-day partial-release evidence (v2026.08.28, v2026.08.29, v2026.08.31 published to npm with no GitHub Release while the newest GitHub Release was v2026.08.17) is encoded as a fixture. Reverting the audit logic to a no-op turns 6 defect-detecting tests red.
